title: Evolith Core Inheritance Rules
description: Rules governing how satellite repositories inherit governance, architecture, and SDLC rules from Evolith Core. Satellites cannot modify Core rules.

principles.statement: Evolith Core rulesets are immutable once published. Satellites inherit rules; they do not fork, modify, or override Core rules.
principles.rationale: If satellites could modify Core rules, the corporate governance baseline would fragment. Federated governance requires a single source of truth.
principles.enforcement: Evolith CLI validates satellite rulesets against Core version. Satellites cannot publish their own rulesets/ directory.

principles.statement: Satellites MUST pin to a specific Core version (coreRef.version) in their evolith.yaml. Unpinned or 'latest' references are prohibited.
principles.rationale: Version pinning ensures reproducible governance. 'Latest' creates drift where different satellites run different rule versions.
principles.enforcement: evolith-yaml.schema.json requires semver version in coreRef.version. CLI warns on missing pin.

principles.statement: Satellite governance version can only increase. Downgrading to an older version requires Architecture Board exception.
principles.rationale: Governance downgrade creates compliance gaps. Exception process ensures downgrade is deliberate and documented.
principles.enforcement: CLI tracks governance version history. Downgrade triggers warning and requires --force flag with justification.

principles.statement: Satellites can define local ADRs for decisions not yet promoted to Core. These are tracked in evolith.yaml compliance.adrRegistry.
principles.rationale: Not every decision needs to be corporate. Satellites have local autonomy for product-specific choices, tracked separately from Core ADRs.
principles.enforcement: Local ADRs must haveEvolithSatellite tag in frontmatter. They are not subject to Core immutability rules.

principles.statement: Local ADR promotion to Core requires Architecture Board review. Evidence from satellite implementation is required.
principles.rationale: Core ADRs must be validated across multiple contexts before being elevated. Single-satellite evidence is insufficient.
principles.enforcement: Promotion request includes: original satellite ADR, evidence of adoption, list of other satellites that could benefit.

principles.statement: Satellite repositories MUST contain a DECISIONS.md file in their root directory to explicitly declare their architecture inheritance contract.
principles.rationale: Without DECISIONS.md, architectural divergences and adoption of Core rules remain invisible, creating hidden technical debt.
principles.enforcement: CLI validates the presence of DECISIONS.md in the root directory of all satellites.

inheritanceChain.description: Satellites inherit from Core only. Multi-level inheritance (satellite → satellite) is prohibited unless explicitly approved by Architecture Board.

levels.name: Evolith Core
levels.description: Source of truth for all governance, architecture, and SDLC rules. Only place where rulesets/ and schema/ are authoritative.

levels.name: Satellite Repository
levels.description: Inherits Core rules via evolith.yaml. Cannot modify Core. Can define local ADRs and extend within allowed boundaries.

prohibited: Satellite → Satellite inheritance (without Architecture Board exception)
Satellite modifying Core rulesets/ or schema/
Core referencing satellite rules as authoritative

steps.action: Evolith CLI notifies satellite of new Core version
Satellite owner reviews changelog between current and new version
Update evolith.yaml coreRef.version to new version
Run CI validation against new ruleset version
Fix any rule violations introduced by upgrade
Architecture Board reviews if breaking changes affected bounded contexts

upgradeProcess.breakGlass: Emergency Core patches (security, legal) can be fast-tracked with Technology Director approval and immediate satellite notification.
